model.architecture: Granite 4.0-h is IBM's hybrid architecture: Mamba2 (selective-scan) blocks interleaved with a few grouped-query attention blocks (this 1B/1.5B-class model has 36 mamba + 4 attention layers).

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic on linears + embedding (convs and the selective scan stay float)

recommended.reason: the Android path measured on a Pixel 8a (Tensor G3): 9.4-9.6 tok/s decode on gpu; the same phone's cpu row decodes 5.0-10.0 tok/s

measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 24.95 tok/s decode / 231.1 prefill, peak 2944 MB, init 15.9 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-24, 1 run) against CPU 23.66-29.39 decode / 129.4-178.7 prefill, peak 2605 MB, init 3.0 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken: decode is a wash (within 10%); gpu is kept for its prefill advantage (time to first token), a deliberate choice rather than a decode win

platform_notes: GPU execution verified on macOS (Metal), iPhone 17 Pro (Metal), Pixel 8a (Arm Mali, OpenCL) and Qualcomm Adreno (Galaxy S26).
GPU inference runs with fp32 activations (bundle declares prefer_activation_type = fp32); that is where the GPU rows' extra memory goes — 2.53 GB vs 0.99 GB on iPhone.
On low-end Android the GPU does not win decode but still wins prefill and TTFT; on Apple hardware the GPU wins across the board.
Pixel 8a: GPU wins prefill (~1.7x) and TTFT and holds a steadier decode; full delegation, zero rejected ops, correct output.
The scan stays unquantized (float); int8 covers linears + embedding.
Multi-length prefill signatures (1–1024) exported; bundle carries Granite's full chat template (tool-calling and RAG-documents sections included).
Mamba blocks carry constant-size per-layer state so memory stays nearly flat with context length; only the 4 attention layers keep KV (4096-token budget).
litert-lm >= 0.15 binds per-layer states through an ExecutorMetadata section appended at package time.
